title: S6 Econ Micro Quiz Revision — 28 Sep 2026
subject: Economics
description: Tomorrow's microeconomics quiz revision set, converted from the uploaded “S6 Econ micro definitions ans (2026-27)” sheet. Wording follows the source answers.

items.prompt: Explain positive statement & normative statement.
items.answer: Positive statement is refutable by fact. Normative statement is not refutable by fact.

items.prompt: Draw / explain the circular flow model of economic activities.
items.answer: Product market: firms provide final goods and services to households; households' consumption expenditure becomes firms' revenue. Factor market: households provide factors of production to firms; firms' cost of production becomes households' factor income. Real flow and money flow move in opposite directions.

items.prompt: Explain 3 basic economic problems.
items.answer: What to produce: type/quantity of goods. How to produce: production method. For whom to produce: criteria of who can enjoy the good/service.

items.prompt: What are private property rights?
items.answer: Exclusive right to use the good; exclusive right to receive income generated by the use of the good; right to transfer the good.

items.prompt: Explain economic good & free good.
items.answer: Economic good: more of it is preferred. Free good: more of it is not preferred.

items.prompt: Explain producer good & consumer good.
items.answer: Producer good: used to produce other good/service. Consumer good: used to satisfy wants directly.

items.prompt: Explain public good & private good.
items.answer: Public good: non-rival in consumption; one's consumption will not reduce the amount available to others. Private good: rival in consumption; one's consumption will reduce the amount available to others.

items.prompt: Give 3 advantages of division of labour / specialisation.
items.answer: Assign suitable worker to the right job — the worker is good at that job. Practice makes perfect — workers become skilful from repeating the same task. Save time in training — workers don't need to learn the whole production.

items.prompt: Explain 3 types of division of labour / specialisation.
items.answer: Simple: concentrate in producing different goods/services. Complex: concentrate in different production processes of the same good / play different roles in teamwork. Regional: workers in different regions concentrate in producing different goods/services or production process of the same good.

items.prompt: Give 3 disadvantages of division of labour / specialisation.
items.answer: Boring / monotonous work — workers repeat day after day. Higher risk of unemployment — limited skills of workers. Loss of job satisfaction — difficult to recognise contribution.

items.prompt: Explain 3 types of production.
items.answer: Primary: extract natural resources to produce raw materials. Secondary: turn raw materials into semi-finished or finished goods. Tertiary: provide services.

items.prompt: Explain 4 types of factor of production.
items.answer: Capital: man-made resources used in production. Land: natural resources used in production. Labour: physical and mental human effort used in production. Entrepreneurship: bear business risks and make major production decisions.

items.prompt: Write equation of labour supply & labour productivity.
items.answer: Labour supply = Number of workers × Average working hours. Labour productivity = Total output / Total working hours.

items.prompt: Explain 2 types of labour mobility.
items.answer: Occupational mobility: willingness and ease of labour to change from one occupation to another. Geographical mobility: willingness and ease of labour to change from one working area to another.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages of time rate compared to piece rate for employer.
items.answer: Lower cost of measuring output. Lower cost of monitoring product quality — workers don't have to hurry.

items.prompt: Explain 1 advantage of piece rate compared to time rate for employer.
items.answer: Lower cost of monitoring workers' performance — increase workers' incentive to work.

items.prompt: Give 1 advantage and 1 disadvantage of profit-sharing scheme compared to time rate for employer.
items.answer: Advantage: transferring some business risks to workers — less wage payment when poor business. Disadvantage: more difficult to recruit workers.

items.prompt: Give 1 advantage and 1 disadvantage of piece rate compared to time rate for employee.
items.answer: Advantage: higher income with more effort. Disadvantage: unstable income.

items.prompt: Explain fixed factor & variable cost.
items.answer: Fixed factor: quantity does not change when output changes. Variable cost: cost increases when output increases.

items.prompt: Explain short run & long run.
items.answer: Short run: there are fixed factors and variable factors. Long run: there are only variable factors, but no fixed factors.

items.prompt: State law of diminishing marginal returns.
items.answer: In the short run, when more variable factors are continuously added to a given quantity of fixed factors, marginal product of the variable factor will eventually decrease, holding technology constant.

items.prompt: Explain 3 reasons for internal economies of scale.
items.answer: A larger firm can borrow from banks at a lower interest rate because creditworthiness increases, lowering average borrowing cost. It can buy inputs in bulk for a larger discount, lowering average input cost. It can spread advertising cost over larger output, lowering average advertising cost.

items.prompt: Explain 2 reasons for external economies of scale.
items.answer: A larger industry can attract more experienced and skilled workers, lowering average recruiting cost. A larger industry can attract more buyers, lowering average marketing cost.

items.prompt: Explain 2 reasons for internal diseconomies of scale.
items.answer: A firm which is too large may need to pay a higher interest rate after borrowing too much, increasing average borrowing cost. It may have lower managerial efficiency because its organization becomes too complicated, increasing average management cost.

items.prompt: Explain 2 reasons for external diseconomies of scale.
items.answer: An industry which is too large may need to develop new markets because existing markets are saturated, increasing average marketing cost. It may suffer higher input costs because of large demand for inputs, increasing average purchasing cost.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages of company issuing shares instead of bonds.
items.answer: Issuing shares has no interest burden, while issuing bonds has. Issuing shares has no redemption obligation, while issuing bonds has.

items.prompt: Give 2 disadvantages of company issuing shares instead of bonds.
items.answer: Issuing shares will dilute existing shareholders' control rights, while issuing bonds will not. Issuing shares has higher risk of being taken over than issuing bonds.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages of investors buying shares instead of bonds.
items.answer: Investors buying shares have voting rights in shareholders' meeting, while buying bonds does not. Investors may have higher return if company earns a lot of profits.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages of investors buying bonds instead of shares.
items.answer: Investors will have more stable return. Investors have higher priority in getting capital back if company liquidates.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages and 2 disadvantages of partnership compared to private limited company.
items.answer: Advantages: lower profits tax rate with same amount of profits; more simple and inexpensive set-up procedures. Disadvantages: partnership owners bear unlimited liability while private limited company owners bear limited liability; partnership lacks continuity while private limited company has lasting continuity.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages and 2 disadvantages of sole proprietorship compared to partnership.
items.answer: Advantages: sole proprietorship can freely transfer ownership, while partnership needs consent of other owners; more flexible decision-making because no need to consult other owners. Disadvantages: narrower source of capital; no specialization in management, while partnership has.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages and 2 disadvantages of private limited company compared to public limited company.
items.answer: Advantages: private limited company does not need to disclose financial information to the public; lower risk of being taken over. Disadvantages: needs consent of other owners to transfer ownership while public limited company has freely transferable ownership; cannot invite public subscription for shares while public limited company can.

items.prompt: Give 2 advantages and 2 disadvantages of public enterprise compared to private enterprise.
items.answer: Advantages: easier to get information about the general public; easier to get loan with the backup of the government. Disadvantages: weaker incentives to improve efficiency; weaker incentives to improve quality of goods/services.

items.prompt: Explain 5 types of expansion.
items.answer: Horizontal: expands into same production stage of the same product. Vertical backward: preceding production stage of the same product. Vertical forward: later production stage of the same product. Lateral: related but not competing product. Conglomerate: unrelated product.

items.prompt: Give 2 motives of 5 types of expansion.
items.answer: All types: economies of scale, e.g. a larger firm can buy inputs in bulk for a larger discount. Horizontal: increase market share. Vertical backward: secure steady input supply. Vertical forward: secure market outlet. Lateral: make use of brand name to sell other products. Conglomerate: spread risk through product diversification.

items.prompt: Give 3 features of 4 types of market structure.
items.answer: Perfect competition: homogeneous product, perfect market information, price taker. Monopolistic competition: many small sellers, free entry and exit, imperfect market information. Oligopoly: few large sellers, interdependence in pricing policies, imperfect market information. Monopoly: one seller, price searcher, imperfect market information.

items.prompt: Give a source of monopoly power.
items.answer: Natural monopoly / Government monopoly.

items.prompt: State law of demand & law of supply.
items.answer: Law of demand: when (relative) price increases, (relative) quantity demanded will decrease, ceteris paribus, vice versa. Law of supply: when price increases, quantity supplied will increase, ceteris paribus, vice versa.

items.prompt: Explain excess demand & excess supply.
items.answer: Excess demand: when market price is lower than equilibrium price, quantity demanded is larger than quantity supplied. Excess supply: when market price is higher than equilibrium price, quantity supplied is larger than quantity demanded.

items.prompt: Write equation of consumer surplus, producer surplus & total social surplus.
items.answer: Consumer surplus = sum of (marginal benefit - price) = total benefit - total expenditure. Producer surplus = sum of (price - marginal cost) = total revenue - total variable cost. Total social surplus = sum of (marginal benefit - marginal cost) = total benefit - total variable cost.

items.prompt: Write equation of profit.
items.answer: Profit = Total revenue - Total cost = [P × Q] - [Total Fixed cost + Total Variable cost].

items.prompt: Explain 2 functions of price.
items.answer: Rationing: goods are distributed to the highest-valued consumers. Allocative: producers direct more resources to produce goods/services with higher prices.

items.prompt: Explain inefficiency caused by externality.
items.answer: Marginal (social) benefit is larger / smaller than marginal (social) cost. Equilibrium/current quantity is smaller / larger than efficient output.

items.prompt: Explain 2 sources of income inequality.
items.answer: Difference in education level / physical attributes: people with better education / physical attributes can earn higher income. Gender discrimination: female earns lower income.

items.prompt: Explain 2 reasons for difference in income inequality.
items.answer: More homogeneous human capital, less income inequality. Difference in wage payment method: time rates cause less income inequality while commissions cause greater income inequality.
